# 2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game

The **2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game** was a National Football League (NFL) regular season contest played on December 15, 2013, at AT\&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. The game featured the **Green Bay Packers** (7-6-1) defeating the **Dallas Cowboys** (7-7) by a score of **37-36** in one of the most dramatic comebacks in NFL history . The Packers overcame a **23-point halftime deficit** (26-3) to secure victory, matching the largest comeback in franchise history .

## Game background and context

The game was significant for both teams' playoff aspirations. The Packers, despite missing their starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers who suffered a broken collarbone in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears , entered the contest with a 7-6-1 record, trailing the 8-6 Chicago Bears in the NFC North division . The Cowboys, with a 7-7 record, were chasing the 8-6 Philadelphia Eagles in the NFC East division .

The Packers were led by backup quarterback **Matt Flynn**, who was making his second consecutive start in place of the injured Rodgers . The Cowboys were coached by Jason Garrett and featured quarterback Tony Romo, who was playing with a herniated disc in his lower back .

## Game summary

### First half

The first half belonged entirely to the Cowboys, who dominated both sides of the ball. The Cowboys scored on their opening drive, with kicker Dan Bailey converting a 47-yard field goal at 10:56 of the first quarter . The Packers responded with a long field goal of their own, as Mason Crosby connected on a 57-yard attempt at 7:40 .

The Cowboys then took control, scoring 20 unanswered points. Bailey added field goals of 23, 43, and 50 yards , while quarterback Tony Romo threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to tight end Jason Witten at the end of the first quarter . Running back DeMarco Murray capped the first-half scoring with a 1-yard touchdown run with 24 seconds left in the second quarter, giving the Cowboys a commanding 26-3 lead at halftime .

### Second half

The Packers came out of halftime with renewed energy and immediately struck back. On the first play of the third quarter, rookie running back **Eddie Lacy** burst through the line for a 60-yard run . Three plays later, Matt Flynn connected with wide receiver Jordy Nelson on a 13-yard touchdown pass, cutting the deficit to 26-10 .

The Cowboys added a field goal early in the fourth quarter to extend their lead to 29-17 , but the Packers' comeback was just beginning. Flynn led the Packers on a remarkable second-half performance, throwing four touchdown passes in the final two quarters . He connected with tight end Andrew Quarless (3 yards), running back James Starks (11 yards), and wide receiver James Jones (3 yards) for touchdowns .

### Fourth quarter and final minutes

With the score tied at 29-29 early in the fourth quarter, the Cowboys appeared to have sealed the victory when Romo threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Dez Bryant, giving them a 36-29 lead with 7:55 remaining .

However, the Packers refused to quit. Flynn engineered another touchdown drive, culminating in a 3-yard touchdown pass to James Jones with 4:17 left, cutting the deficit to 36-31 .

The decisive moment came with 2:58 remaining when the Cowboys were attempting to run out the clock. Facing a second-and-6 from their own 35-yard line, Romo threw an interception to Packers cornerback **Sam Shields** . The Packers capitalized on the turnover, driving 50 yards in seven plays. Eddie Lacy scored the game-winning touchdown on a 1-yard run with 1:31 remaining . The Packers failed on the two-point conversion attempt, leaving the score at 37-36 .

On the Cowboys' ensuing drive, Romo was intercepted again, this time by Packers cornerback **Tramon Williams** on the second play, effectively ending the game .

## Key players and performances

### Green Bay Packers

**Matt Flynn** delivered a remarkable second-half performance, completing 26 of 39 passes for 299 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception . His quarterback rating of 113.1 was particularly impressive given that he had struggled in his previous start on Thanksgiving Day . Flynn's four touchdown passes in the second half matched the Packers' largest comeback in franchise history .

**Eddie Lacy** had a monster game, rushing for 141 yards on 21 carries, including the game-winning 1-yard touchdown run . His 60-yard run on the first play of the second half provided the spark the Packers needed to begin their comeback .

The Packers' defense, despite giving up 26 points in the first half, made crucial plays when needed. Cornerbacks Sam Shields and Tramon Williams each recorded interceptions in the final three minutes of the game . Shields had a particularly outstanding game, surrendering just four catches for 67 yards in 10 targets, with three pass breakups .

### Dallas Cowboys

**Tony Romo** completed 29 of 48 passes for 358 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions . While his two late interceptions proved costly, Romo had several impressive throws throughout the game, including a 25-yard touchdown pass to Jason Witten and a 5-yard touchdown pass to Dez Bryant .

**DeMarco Murray** was highly effective on the ground, rushing for 134 yards on 18 carries at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt . His 1-yard touchdown run in the second quarter gave the Cowboys their 23-point halftime lead .

**Dez Bryant** was the Cowboys' leading receiver with 11 catches for 153 yards and one touchdown . However, his decision to walk off the field while there was still time remaining in the game drew criticism .

**Jason Witten** caught four passes for 71 yards and one touchdown, extending his streak of consecutive games with at least one reception to 85 games .

## Coaching decisions and controversies

The game was marred by several controversial coaching decisions, particularly by Cowboys head coach Jason Garrett. Despite having a 23-point halftime lead and an effective running game (DeMarco Murray averaged 7.4 yards per carry), the Cowboys failed to run the ball effectively in the second half . Murray had 83 yards on 11 carries in the first half but received only seven more touches in the second half .

Garrett's decision to use a "smoke" or "flash" play (a run play with a pass option) on the Cowboys' penultimate drive also drew criticism. With the Cowboys leading 36-31 and attempting to run out the clock, Romo was instructed to throw if the Packers stacked the box against the run . When Romo saw eight Packers defenders in the box, he threw the pass, which was intercepted by Sam Shields .

After the game, Garrett appeared to place blame on Romo, stating that Romo "probably should have run the ball" on the play . However, this was widely viewed as a disingenuous attempt to deflect criticism, as the play was designed to become a pass if the defense stacked the box .

## Game significance

The Packers' victory was significant for several reasons. First, it kept their playoff hopes alive, as they remained one game behind the Chicago Bears in the NFC North division . Second, it marked the largest comeback in Packers franchise history, matching their previous record set in 1945 .

For the Cowboys, the loss had devastating implications. Not only did it eliminate their chances of winning the NFC East division title outright, but it also damaged their wild-card playoff hopes . The defeat was seen as another example of the Cowboys' inability to close out games and was particularly damaging to coach Jason Garrett's reputation .

The game also highlighted the importance of having quality depth at the quarterback position. Despite missing their franchise quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the Packers were able to win with backup Matt Flynn, who had been widely criticized after a poor performance on Thanksgiving .

## Conclusion

The 2013 Green Bay Packers–Dallas Cowboys game will be remembered as one of the most dramatic comebacks in NFL history. The Packers' ability to overcome a 23-point halftime deficit to win 37-36 demonstrated remarkable resilience and determination. Matt Flynn's four touchdown passes in the second half, combined with Eddie Lacy's game-winning touchdown run, secured a memorable victory for the Packers.

For the Cowboys, the game represented another missed opportunity and highlighted ongoing issues with coaching decisions and the defense's inability to protect leads. Tony Romo's two late interceptions, while certainly contributing to the loss, were not the sole reason for the defeat. The Cowboys' failure to run the ball effectively in the second half and their defense's inability to stop the Packers' comeback proved costly.

The game had significant implications for both teams' playoff aspirations. While the Packers went on to win their next game and secure a wild-card berth, they were eliminated in the first round by the San Francisco 49ers. The Cowboys, meanwhile, lost their next game and were eliminated from playoff contention, finishing with an 8-8 record for the third consecutive season.

The 2013 Packers-Cowboys game stands as a testament to the unpredictable nature of professional football and the importance of playing a full 60 minutes. It will long be remembered as one of the most exciting games of the 2013 NFL season.

CowBuzz: Behind The Scenes Of Cowboys vs Packers
================================================

![Image 3: Author Image](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_thumb_squared/f_auto/cowboys/t4corpynuc2pko82j7wg.jpg)

[Shannon Gross](https://www.dallascowboys.com/author/shannon-gross)

*   Copied!

![Image 4: cowbuzz121513.png](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_png/cowboys/mdvsjgsvew1wigsdqvcv.png)

Dan Bailey converted all five field goal tries today to give him 85 career field goals and pass Chris Boniol (81) for second in team history. Two of Bailey's field goals were 50-yarders, giving him six field goals of 50-or-more yards made this season to establish a club record. He was tied with Ken Willis (1991) and David Buehler (2010) coming into today's game. For his career, Bailey now has 11 field goals of 50-or-more yards to extend his club record. His five field goals today also gave Bailey his third career four-plus field goal game to tie Chris Boniol for the most in club history. Bailey has two games with five-or-more field goals to tie Chris Boniol and Richie Cunningham for the most in franchise history. His five also tied the third-most in a game in franchise history.

Dez Bryant finished today's game with 11 catches for 153 yards and a touchdown.

Bryant now has 11 touchdown receptions this season to tie the eighth-most in a season in franchise history. For his career Bryant has 38 touchdown catches to tie Terrell Owens for eighth in team history. Bryant upped his career receptions total to 281 to tie Frank Clarke for 12th in team history.

DeMarco Murray rushed 18 times for 134 yards and a touchdown today. His 18 rushes upped his career rushing carries to 503 and made him the 13th Dallas Cowboy with 500 career rushing attempts. Murray's 134 yards gave him his third 100-yard game of the season and the seventh of his career. The 134 yards were sixth in a game in his career. For his career, Murray has 2,537 rushing yards – the 11th Dallas Cowboy to cross the 2,500-yard threshold. Murray's rushing score today was his eighth of the season – the most by a Cowboy since Marion Barber had 10 in 2007.

Jason Witten appeared in his 169th straight game today. His 169 consecutive games played are third in team history. Dale Hellestrae (176, 1990-2000) and Bob Lilly (196, 1961-74) hold the top-two spots.

With his four catches for 71 yards and one touchdown today, Witten has now caught at least one pass in 85 straight games and trails only Michael Irvin (117 from 1990-98) for the team record. Witten's last game without a reception was at the N.Y. Giants (11/2/08). Witten now has 865 career catches to pass Jimmy Smith (862) for 17th in league history. Witten caught a touchdown pass for his eighth score of the season. Witten's eight are second in a season in his career (nine in 2010) and gave him 52 career touchdown catches – third in Cowboys history and tied with Dave Casper and Vernon Davis for seventh among NFL tight ends.

Witten now has sole possession of third in touchdowns in Cowboys history, breaking a tie with Tony Hill.

Green Bay Packers tight end Andrew Quarless (81) scores a touchdown as Dallas Cowboys outside linebacker Cameron Lawrence (53) and Sterling Moore (26) defends during the second half of an NFL football game, Sunday, Dec. 15, 2013, in Arlington, Texas. (AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)

Tony Gutierrez

In an unbelievable rally, the visiting Packers stormed back from a 23-point halftime deficit to stun the Cowboys 37-36 at AT&T Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The victory keeps the Packers (7-6-1) a half-game behind the Bears (8-6) with two games left to play. It also adds to the pressure on Detroit, which hosts Baltimore on Sunday night.

From a standings standpoint, the defeat keeps Dallas (7-7) from drawing even with Philadelphia (8-6) in the NFC East.

However, this could be a setback with much greater meaning and impact for the Cowboys.

For Dallas, this marks yet another lamentable performance by its defense, which allowed five second-half TDs to Green Bay.

Also, Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo was intercepted on each of Dallas’ last two drives — once with Dallas holding a 36-31 lead and trying to run out the clock, and once with Dallas trying to put together a last-ditch comeback in the final minute.

On the first interception, Romo eluded pressure from the rush, then threw over the middle for Miles Austin. However, Packers cornerback Sam Shields intercepted the pass — and it’s a good thing for Green Bay that he did, for Shields was the last line of defense.

The pick gave the Packers the ball at midfield, and from there, they embarked on a seven-play march ending in Eddie Lacy’s one-yard TD run with 91 seconds left to give Green Bay the final margin of victory.

On the second play of Dallas’ ensuing drive, Romo was picked again, this time by Packers cornerback Tramon Williams, and Green Bay had secured a most memorable triumph.

Packers quarterback Matt Flynn threw for 182 yards and four touchdowns in the final two quarters, connecting with wideout Jordy Nelson (13 yards), tight end Andrew Quarless (three yards), running back James Starks (11 yards) and wideout James Jones (three yards) for scores. On three separate occasions, the Packers put together 80-yard drives ending in Flynn TD passes.

The Packers’ out-of-nowhere closing kick came after a horrid first half, one that saw the Cowboys build a 26-3 lead. The Cowboys’ offense was far too much for the Packers’ defense to handle in all areas, and the Cowboys’ defense — picked apart six days earlier at Chicago — stood up for itself, limiting Green Bay to just a 57-yard field goal.

Frankly, the Cowboys looked home free as the third quarter started. Then, on the first play of the second half, Lacy rumbled for 60 yards off left tackle. Three plays later, Flynn hit Nelson for six points. The Packers had the quick touchdown they needed.

As it turns out, they were far from finished.

Now, the attention turns to how the Cowboys respond after being caught near the wire. Thus begins a long, long week of discussion of Romo’s legacy, of the defense’s shortcomings, of what it all means to a franchise that hasn’t won a division title since 2009.

Still, with a win Sunday at Washington, Dallas will have a shot at the NFC East title no matter how Philadelphia fares against Chicago next Sunday night. If the Cowboys win the next their two games, they win the division.

First, though, they need to shake this one off.

Date December 15, 2013
Stadium[AT&T Stadium](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium "AT&T Stadium"), Arlington, Texas
[Referee](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Official_(American_football) "Official (American football)")[Walt Coleman](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Walt_Coleman "Walt Coleman")

TV in the United States
Network Fox
Announcers[Joe Buck](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Joe_Buck "Joe Buck"), [Troy Aikman](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Troy_Aikman "Troy Aikman"), and Pam Oliver

The [Green Bay Packers](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") played the [Dallas Cowboys](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") in Week 15 of the [2013 NFL season](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_NFL_season "2013 NFL season") on December 15, 2013, at [AT&T Stadium](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium "AT&T Stadium") in Arlington, Texas. Both teams entered Week 15 with middling records, with the Packers sitting at 6–6–1 and the Cowboys at 7–6. The Packers started the season strong, yet a broken collarbone by quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") in Week 8 saw the Packers lose or tie five straight games under three different back-up quarterbacks. Both teams were coming off a loss in Week 14, although each of their respective playoff hopes were still alive and both still had a chance to win their respective divisions.

The Cowboys started the game strong, taking a 26-3 lead going into halftime, with kicker [Dan Bailey](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Dan_Bailey "Dan Bailey") converting four field goals. [Matt Flynn](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Flynn "Matt Flynn"), who was playing in place of the injured Rodgers, helped the Packers storm back in the second half. He led the Packers to five touchdown drives, including four touchdown passes. The Packers defense was able to hold the Cowboys to just 10 points in the second half, with Tramon Williams sealing the victory with an interception of quarterback [Tony Romo](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") with less than two minutes left in the game. The victory matched the Packers team record for the largest comeback at 23 points and helped them maintain the possibility of winning the [NFC North](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/NFC_North "NFC North") and making the playoffs. Both teams entered the final week of the season with a chance to win their division; the Packers won, while the Cowboys lost. The Packers would make the playoffs yet lose in the first round to the [San Francisco 49ers](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers").

*   **Main article:**_[2013 Green Bay Packers](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013\_Green\_Bay\_Packers "2013 Green Bay Packers")_

The [Green Bay Packers](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") began the season as the defending [NFC North](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/NFC_North "NFC North") champions, having won the division the previous two seasons.[[1]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-1) They began their season with a record of 5–2, although one of their losses came after surrendering a 16-point second half lead to the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals").[[2]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-2013PACK-2)[[3]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-3) Their eighth game of the year was on _[Monday Night Football](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Monday\_Night\_Football "Monday Night Football")_ against the [Chicago Bears](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"). In the first quarter, [Aaron Rodgers](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") was injured, missing the rest of the game with what was later diagnosed as a broken collarbone.[[4]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-4) Rodgers would go on to miss the next seven games, with Seneca Wallace, [Scott Tolzien](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Scott_Tolzien "Scott Tolzien"), and [Matt Flynn](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Flynn "Matt Flynn") all starting games in his place. Wallace was injured in his first game and the Packers signed Flynn, who had played for the Packers previously, midway through the season. The Packers went 0–4–1 during a five-game stretch which included the Bears game to bring their record to 5–6–1.[[2]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-2013PACK-2) The Packers played the [Atlanta Falcons](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons") in Week 14 and feel behind 21–10 in the first half. However, Flynn led a comeback to beat the Falcons 22–21, evening the Packers record at 6–6–1 and keeping them in the hunt for the NFC North.[[5]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-5)

The [Dallas Cowboys](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") began the 2013 season having gone 8–8 in back-to-back seasons, missing the playoffs both times.[[6]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-6) The season was back-and-forth, with the Cowboys never winning more than two games in a row nor losing more than two games in a row. They entered Week 15 with a record of 7–6 after a loss to the Bears in Week 14.[[7]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-2013COW-7) The Cowboys were scheduled to host the Packers in Week 15 at [AT&T Stadium](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/AT%26T_Stadium "AT&T Stadium") on December 15, 2013. Both teams were mathematically still in the hunt for their respective division titles.[[8]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-8)

### First half[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Famericanfootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D3&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

The Cowboys started the game with possession of the ball. A 27-yard pass from [Tony Romo](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Tony_Romo "Tony Romo") to Terrance Williams got the Cowboys in scoring position, but the Packers got a stop on third down and forced a 47-yard field goal attempt, which [Dan Bailey](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Dan_Bailey "Dan Bailey") converted. The Packers matched the Cowboys on the next drive, going 41 yards in 6 plays to set-up a 57-yard field goal attempt. Almost all of the yardage on the drive came from a 39-yard pass from [Matt Flynn](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Flynn "Matt Flynn") to James Jones. [Mason Crosby](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Mason_Crosby "Mason Crosby") converted the field goa, tying the game at 3–3. On the subsequent drive, Demarco Murray had a 41-yard rush that put the Cowboys in scoring position, but again the Packers stopped the Cowboys on third down, with Bailey converting a 23-yard field goal to give the Cowboys the lead again, 6–3. After the Packers went three-and-out and punted, the Cowboys quickly drove 65 yards in 4 plays, capped off by a 25-yard touchdown from Romo to [Jason Witten](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Jason_Witten "Jason Witten"). The Cowboys lead increased to 13–3. On the first play of the next drive, Flynn threw deep to Jones and the Cowboys were called for a 31-yard defensive pass interference penalty. However, after a sack and two incomplete passes, the Packers were forced to punt again. Each team then exchanged punts after short drives. The Cowboys got the ball back and drove 48 yards in 8 plays, but again were stopped and had to attempt a field goal. Bailey converted his third field goal of the half, this time from 43 yards, to increase the Cowboys lead to 16–3. On the next drive, Flynn threw an interception to Sterling Moore, who returned it 21 yards. The Packers did not allow the Cowboys to gain any yardage on their drive, but they were already in field goal range. Bailey made his fourth field goal of the half, this time from 50 yards, bringing the score to 19–3. The Packers were again forced to punt on their next drive. Romo completed three passes on the next drive for a combined 70 yards, with Murray scoring a touchdown on a one-yard rush. The Packers attempted to score on the next drive, but they ran out of a time after a 34-yard screen pass from Flynn to [Eddie Lacy](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Eddie_Lacy "Eddie Lacy") ended the first half. The Cowboys led 26–3 at halftime.[[9]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-PLAYBYPLAY-9)

### Second half[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Famericanfootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

The Packers had possession of the ball to begin the second half. On the first play of their drive, Lacy had a 60-yard rush; three plays later Flynn threw a touchdown pass to [Jordy Nelson](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Jordy_Nelson "Jordy Nelson"), cutting the Cowboys lead to 26–10. The Cowboys responded, with Bailey kicking his fifth field goal, from 50 yards, of the game after an 11-play, 48-yard drive. On the ensuing drive, the Packers again travelled the length of the field, going 80 yards in 12 plays, and scoring on a 3-yard touchdown pass from Flynn to Andrew Quarless. After the Cowboys' field goal and Packers' touchdown, the score was 29–17. The Packers forced a three-and-out on the Cowboys' next drive after sacking Romo on third down. [Micah Hyde](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Micah_Hyde "Micah Hyde") returned the Cowboys' punt from mid-field 26 yards. The Packers scored five plays later on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Flynn to [James Starks](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/James_Starks "James Starks"). The Cowboys lead was now only five points, 29–24. On the Cowboys next drive, Romo threw a pass that appeared to be intercepted by Tramon Williams, however after replay review, the pass was called incomplete. The Cowboys capitalized, going the length of the field to score a touchdown on a short pass from Romo to [Dez Bryant](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Dez_Bryant "Dez Bryant"). The Packers responded, going 80 yards in 10 plays to score, with Flynn completing a 3-yard pass to Jones for a touchdown. The Cowboys lead was cut back to five points again, with the score at 36–31. The Cowboys converted a third down with 12 yards to go on the next drive, but on the fifth play Romo threw an interception to Sam Shields at mid-field. The Packers drove to the Cowboys' one-yard line with less than two minutes left in the game. Lacy scored a touchdown on a one-yard rush, with the Packers failing on the two-point conversion. Down for the first time in the game, 37–36, the Cowboys began their next drive with a nine-yard completion from Romo to Cole Beasley. Romo's next pass was ruled incomplete, yet after replay review, the call was changed to an interception by Williams. The Packers ran out the rest of the game clock to secure the comeback victory.[[9]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-PLAYBYPLAY-9)

### Analysis[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Famericanfootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D6&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

[File:Matt Flynn 10 Barking Signals Dec 2013.jpg](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Special:Upload?wpDestFile=Matt_Flynn_10_Barking_Signals_Dec_2013.jpg "File:Matt Flynn 10 Barking Signals Dec 2013.jpg")

[Matt Flynn](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Flynn "Matt Flynn"), shown here during another 2013 game, helped lead the Packers' comeback with four touchdown passes in the second half.

Post-game analysis focused on the Packers’ comeback and the significant differences for each team between the first and second half.[[12]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-VANDERMAUSE-12)[[13]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-FEELING-13)[[14]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-14) The Packers' offense was only able to score three points in the first half, even though the Cowboys came into the game with the worst ranked defense in the NFL.[[15]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-THICK1-15)[[16]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-THICK2-16) The Packers' defense was able to stop the Cowboys offense on four drives, forcing field goals instead of touchdowns.[[10]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-PFRBOX-10) Even so, the Cowboys offense was able to move the ball through the air and on the ground and took a commanding 26-3 lead into halftime.[[15]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-THICK1-15)[[16]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-THICK2-16) Coming into the second half, the Packers decided to run the ball, with Lacy breaking free for a 60-yard rush that multiple players noted sparked the Packers’ offense.[[17]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-RUSHING-17) The Packers scored their first touchdown three plays later, starting a streak of five straight touchdown drives.[[13]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-FEELING-13) Other key plays were highlighted, including interceptions in the fourth quarter by Shields and Williams that helped the Packers gain the lead for the first time and seal their victory.[[13]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-FEELING-13)[[12]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-VANDERMAUSE-12)

Individual performances were highlighted, especially on offense. Romo threw for 358 yards and two touchdowns, while Flynn had 299 passing yards and four touchdowns. Each team had a 100-yard rusher, with Lacy gaining 141 yards and Murray having 134 yards; each scored a touchdown.[[18]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-NUMBERS-18) Boykin and Quarless led the Packers in receptions and yards, although Nelson’s performance on third down was specifically noted.[[18]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-NUMBERS-18)[[19]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-NELSON-19) On the Cowboys’ side, Bryant had a successful performance, catching 11 passes for 153 yards and a touchdown.[[18]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-NUMBERS-18) His touchdown catch was praised for its level of difficulty.[[20]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-NFL-20)

After the game, decisions by the Cowboys coaching staff and Romo were questioned..[[20]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-NFL-20) The Cowboys were very successful rushing the ball in the first half, with Murray going for 93 yards. However, in the second half, even with a large lead, the Cowboys only gave the ball to Murray seven times. Ironically, it was the Packers who saw a lot of success in the second half rushing the ball.[[17]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-RUSHING-17) This was very apparent on each Cowboys’ drive that ended in an interception, with post-game commentators questioning why the Cowboys were not trying to run out the clock and instead were throwing the ball downfield.[[20]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-NFL-20)[[21]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-21) Cowboys head coach [Jason Garrett](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Jason_Garrett "Jason Garrett") noted after the game that in hindsight the team should have called more running plays.[[17]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-RUSHING-17)

Aftermath[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Famericanfootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D7&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

After their victory, the Packers record was 7–6–1 and they were still in the hunt for the NFC North title. With Rodgers close to returning, the Packers hosted the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") at [Lambeau Field](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Lambeau_Field "Lambeau Field") in Week 16. In that game the Packers gave up a late score after a fumble by Flynn, but then had a long kickoff return by Micah Hyde. After a couple plays, the Packers got to the one-yard line, but a penalty pushed them back five yards and gave them just enough time to run a play to try to score. Flynn threw incomplete and the Packers lost, leaving them with 7–7–1 record. The Bears lost in Week 16 as well, setting up a match-up in Week 17 for the NFC North title between the Packers and Bears, who were hosting. Rodgers returned from his injury for the Bears game and threw late touchdown pass on fourth down to seal the victory and the NFC North title for the Packers.[[22]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-BEARS-22) The Packers hosted the [San Francisco 49ers](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers") in the first round of the playoffs, [losing 23–30](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_NFL_playoffs#NFC:_San_Francisco_49ers_23,_Green_Bay_Packers_20 "2013–14 NFL playoffs") and ending their season.[[23]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-23)

The Cowboys recovered the next week, beating the [Washington Redskins](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Washington_Redskins "Washington Redskins") and setting up another winner-take-all game for the [NFC East](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/NFC_East "NFC East") division title against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles") in Week 17.[[24]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-24) The Cowboy lost 24-22, with a late interception keeping them from getting into field goal range near the end of the game.[[25]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-MISS-25) The loss gave the Eagles the division title and caused the Cowboys to miss the playoffs for the fourth straight season.[[25]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-MISS-25)[[26]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-26)

### Legacy[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Famericanfootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D8&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

The 23-point comeback victory tied the Packers' record for the largest comeback in franchise history.[[27]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-28) The previous 23-point comeback came during a 1982 regular season game against the Los Angeles Rams. The _Milwaukee Journal Sentinel_ highlighted the game as one of the Packers' biggest fourth quarter comebacks, with the team down 12 points heading into the last quarter.[[29]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-29) It was also the second notable game where Flynn had a big outing as a back-up to Rodgers, after the final game of the 2011 season.[[22]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-BEARS-22) The victory helped the Packers keep their playoffs hopes alive, ultimately becoming necessary for them to win the NFC North.[[30]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-30)[[22]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-BEARS-22) The game is a notable part of the [Cowboys–Packers rivalry](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/Cowboys%E2%80%93Packers_rivalry "Cowboys–Packers rivalry").[[31]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://americanfootball.fandom.com/wiki/2013_Green_Bay_Packers_vs_Dallas_Cowboys#cite_note-32)

ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Matt Flynn threw four touchdown passes in the second half, Eddie Lacy had the winning score on a 1-yard plunge and the Green Bay Packers matched the biggest comeback in franchise history, rallying from 23 points down at halftime to beat the Dallas Cowboys 37-36 Sunday.

Tony Romo had two interceptions in the final 3 minutes, the first one giving Green Bay a chance for the go-ahead score with the Cowboys in position to run out the clock with a 36-31 lead. Lacy scored with just over 1 1-2 minutes left.

Playing on the same field where they won the 2011 Super Bowl, the Packers matched the 1982 team, which rallied past the Los Angeles Rams after trailing by 23.

The Packers (7-6-1) kept their playoff hopes alive with Aaron Rodgers possibly returning next week.

The Cowboys(7-7) stayed a game behind Philadelphia in the NFC East.

Arlington, TX (SportsNetwork.com) - Eddie Lacy's 1-yard touchdown run with 1:31 to play completed an epic Green Bay comeback as the Packers got past the Dallas Cowboys, 37-36.

Trailing by 23 points to start the second half, Green Bay scored touchdowns on its first five possessions of the final 30 minutes, while Tony Romo had another meltdown in the fourth quarter.

With the victory, Green Bay (7-6-1) has managed to stay alive in the chase for the NFC North crown thanks to consecutive wins despite signal-caller Aaron Rodgers still on the sideline as he recovers from a fractured collarbone.

The Packers sit in third place in the NFC North, behind Chicago (8-6) and Detroit (7-6). Detroit hosts the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night.

Matt Flynn, Rodgers' replacement under center, threw for 299 yards and four touchdowns with an interception on 26-of-39 passing, with Lacy finishing the game with 141 yards on 21 carries and a score while adding four catches for 30 yards.

Dallas (7-7), meanwhile, stays a game back of Philadelphia for first place in the NFC East, as the Eagles lost to the Vikings on Sunday.

Romo looked strong for much of the game and went 29-for-48 for 358 yards and two touchdowns overall, but his final two possessions ended in interceptions. The first one led to Lacy's go-ahead score and his second sealed the victory for Green Bay.

DeMarco Murray had another strong game for Dallas, carrying the ball 18 times for 134 yards and a score along with four catches for 19 yards.

Dallas Cowboys continue to feature a flair for the catastrophic
===============================================================

[Judy Battista](https://www.nfl.com/author/judy-battista-0ap1000000233164)

Senior National Columnist

[](https://twitter.com/judybattista)

It is tempting to watch the [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) with a hand over your eyes, peeking through splayed fingers, the way you view a horror movie. The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) are nothing if not that right now, a slowly unspooling _Nightmare In Jerry's World_, starting out innocently enough only to allow the dread to build until it reaches its excruciating, inevitable conclusion.

**On NFL Network**

_NFL Replay_

 will re-air the [Green Bay Packers' 37-36 win](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013121512/2013/REG15/packers@cowboys) over the [Dallas Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) from Week 15 on Wednesday, Dec. 18 at 9 p.m. ET.

» _* [NFL Network schedule](http://www.nfl.com/nflnetwork/networkschedule)_*

These 'Boys have known the feeling that something is about to go terribly wrong so well this season. It is a sense they have honed in recent years, pockmarking an empire -- one that is average in the standings, though highly lucrative nonetheless -- with the painful and pitiful, with the late-game interceptions and late-season meltdowns. It is a feeling that has -- fairly or otherwise -- come to accompany virtually every one of [Tony Romo](https://www.nfl.com/player/tonyromo/2505354/profile)'s drives.

So it was on Sunday afternoon. Even in a season that already has included calamitous [losses to Denver](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013100609/2013/REG5/broncos@cowboys) and [Detroit](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013102700/2013/REG8/cowboys@lions), and last week's [shellacking by Chicago's Josh McCown](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013120900/2013/REG14/cowboys@bears), the way the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) lost to the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) -- ceding a 23-point halftime lead [to fall 37-36](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013121512/2013/REG15/packers@cowboys), to a backup quarterback, at home -- was so cringe-inducing that it felt like a seismic shift, as if the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) were finally coming loose from their moorings.

As Romo threw two late-fourth-quarter interceptions -- one after [he opted to pass instead of run on a packaged play](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000298872/article/jason-garrett-tony-romo-shouldve-handed-off-on-int), even though the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) were trying to bleed the clock and had been running effectively -- as [Dez Bryant walked off the field while there was still time on the clock](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299435/article/dez-bryant-emotional-exits-dallas-cowboys-loss-early), and as a buffet of blame was set up by everyone from Jerry Jones on down, it seemed like anything was possible. With a roster aging at some critical spots, with a coaching staff -- particularly on defense -- incapable of stopping the bleeding, with even the usually sunny Jones burying his inner _Up With People_ and declining to give [Jason Garrett](https://www.nfl.com/player/jasongarrett/2514652/profile) another vote of confidence because, [Jones explained, he already has](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299431/article/jerry-jones-no-need-for-weekly-pledge-to-jason-garrett), darkness has descended over Dallas again and all options suddenly are on the table. Except actually being contenders, even though the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) remain [very much in control of their fate](http://www.nfl.com/playoffs/playoff-picture).

That is a hollow victory for the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL), although they'll probably take any kind of victory right now because there is blame being placed at nearly every locker. Jones noted the lack of impact from [DeMarcus Ware](https://www.nfl.com/player/demarcusware/2506349/profile). Garrett pointed out that Romo should have stuck with a run play on [the fateful first interception](http://www.nfl.com/videos/dallas-cowboys/0ap2000000298715/Romo-s-pass-intercepted-by-Shields). A young receiver cut off his route [on the second interception](http://www.nfl.com/videos/green-bay-packers/0ap2000000298755/Tony-Romo-throws-game-ending-interception).Garrett noted that play-calling is now under [Bill Callahan](https://www.nfl.com/player/billcallahan/2510932/profile)'s auspices.

This is what happens to crumbling teams: Perhaps it's just answering questions honestly, but everybody grasps for a lifeline that is not there.

Romo is the easiest fall guy, and even his most ardent defenders will have trouble excusing Sunday's meltdown. The statistics say he is one of the best fourth-quarter quarterbacks in history, but the perception is that he comes up with gut-wrenching mistakes at the worst possible moments. On Sunday, watching the interceptions, it began to feel like a self-fulfilling prophecy. For three quarters and 12 minutes, he was the quarterback you want. But in those last three minutes, he was the quarterback you fear.

Other QBs threw interceptions in Week 15 that ended their respective teams' chances -- [Tom Brady most prominent among them](http://www.nfl.com/videos/miami-dolphins/0ap2000000298290/Brady-throws-interception-to-end-game). But Brady has not been [outplayed in consecutive games](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013120900/2013/REG14/cowboys@bears) by [backup quarterbacks](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013121512/2013/REG15/packers@cowboys). And the harsh math of the NFL is that if you're going to be [paid like a top-shelf quarterback](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000155364/article/tony-romo-signs-108m-contract-with-dallas-cowboys), you simply must perform like one when the season is on the line.

[Matt Flynn](http://www.nfl.com/voting/never-say-never/2013/REG/15#playerid:0ap2000000298789)

[](http://www.nfl.com/voting/never-say-never/2013/REG/15#playerid:0ap2000000298789)

But of course, Romo should not have had to throw at any point in the second half. The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) moved away from a running game that was working; they had 93 yards rushing in the first half but finished with 134, running just seven times in the second half. And while Romo might have made the critical decision on the first interception, the philosophy of the offense is set by Callahan -- the coordinator to whom Jones handed play-calling duties -- and ultimately Garrett. Late in the third quarter, with the comeback already on, the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) ran the kind of drive that makes you wonder if anybody there deserves to keep their jobs. Romo dropped back three times and failed to get a first down. The drive took exactly 63 seconds off the clock. After the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) scored once more, to close the lead to just five points, the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) took to the air again on the subsequent touchdown drive.

**Schein: All Romo's fault? No way**

![Image 2: _Schein-65x90.jpg](https://static.www.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_auto/league/j8zrwk3taesfmd7kyxrl.jpg)

Everyone blames Tony Romo for the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/_amp/dallas-cowboys-continue-to-feature-a-flair-for-the-catastrophic-0ap2000000299650)' collapse, but **Adam Schein** says the main culprits are higher up in the power structure. [**READ**](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299442/article/tony-romo-gets-heat-what-about-monte-kiffin-jason-garrett)

"The idea was to run the ball and make them use the clock," Garrett said of the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL)' fourth-quarter strategy. "Run it, and then if we have to throw it, throw high-percentage passes to keep the clock going and make them use their timeouts."

Garrett's oddly detached explanation indicates a deeper organizational problem -- that he is either not ultimately responsible or does not feel he can step in to dictate offensive direction if he is unhappy with what Callahan is doing. Only one person can fix that, but Jones is [the person who gave Callahan the play-calling responsibility](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000209080/article/bill-callahan-not-jason-garrett-to-call-cowboys-plays) in the first place.

We know who is in charge of the defense, but Monte Kiffin surely can't be for much longer. Even Jones has admitted in recent weeks that the decision to replace Rob Ryan with Kiffin ["doesn't look good right now."](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000280264/article/jerry-jones-says-rob-ryan-firing-doesnt-look-good) This loss, ultimately, belongs to the growing collection of catastrophic defensive collapses this season. The defense has given up at least 400 yards of offense in eight games, and it is that knowledge -- that the unit cannot preserve a lead, no matter how large -- that is likely informing offensive play-calling that is skewed toward the aggressive.

This, then, is a collective failure. And that, too, is nothing new. After all, when the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) missed the playoffs last season, Jones fired the defensive coordinator and switched offensive play-callers, changes that have borne no fruit.

It is tempting to think the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) are stuck in neutral -- never bottoming out and never improving. But standing still in the NFL is going backward. The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) are slowly decaying, their players getting older, their results getting more galling, their window slamming shut. And Jones already has exercised all of his options for making changes around the margins.

**The playoff picture**

![Image 3: NFL-131103-IA.jpg](https://static.www.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_auto/league/aybck5fv0okrskbroc1p.jpg)

How would your team's prospects look if the season ended today? See where each team stands in the playoff picture midway through the season. [**More ...**](http://www.nfl.com/playoffs/playoff-picture)

The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL), incredibly, still have a chance to win the division, owing to the weakness of the NFC East, but they can't allow that to delude them this offseason into thinking that they are among the league's best teams. They are far from that, and other than Romo -- whose massive contract has conferred untouchability on him -- nobody should feel safe.

On a day of awful decision-making, Jones made one correct call Sunday night. He [did not offer any more votes of confidence](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299431/article/jerry-jones-no-need-for-weekly-pledge-to-jason-garrett), not for any of his coaches or his players. After all, how can anyone who watches the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) be confident in _anything_ anymore -- except knowing that if they uncover their eyes, they are likely to be subjected to a few more hours of scary scenes?

Romo picks punctuate Cowboys' collapse against Packers
======================================================

By [Tom Orsborn](https://www.houstonchronicle.com/author/tom-orsborn/), Sports ReporterUpdated Dec 15, 2013 11:17 p.m.

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/feed?app_id=660176348291138&link=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.houstonchronicle.com%2Fsports%2Farticle%2Fromo-picks-punctuate-cowboys-collapse-against-5067516.php%3Futm_campaign%3DCMS%2520Sharing%2520Tools%2520\(Premium\)%26utm_source%3Dfacebook.com%26utm_medium%3Dreferral&name=Romo%20picks%20punctuate%20Cowboys%27%20collapse%20against%20Packers&description=They%20were%20at%20home%2C%20the%20NFC%20East-leading%20Philadelphia%20Eagles%20had%20lost%20earlier%20in%20the%20day%2C%20and%20the%20visiting%20Green%20Bay%20Packers%20were%20without%20their%20Pro%20Bowl%20quarterback.&picture=https%3A%2F%2Fs.hdnux.com%2Fphotos%2F25%2F30%2F11%2F5603925%2F4%2FrawImage.jpg&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.houstonchronicle.com%2Fsports%2Farticle%2Fromo-picks-punctuate-cowboys-collapse-against-5067516.php%3Futm_campaign%3DCMS%2520Sharing%2520Tools%2520\(Premium\)%26utm_source%3DUTMSOURCE%26utm_medium%3DUTMMEDIUM)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.houstonchronicle.com%2Fsports%2Farticle%2Fromo-picks-punctuate-cowboys-collapse-against-5067516.php%3Futm_campaign%3DCMS%2520Sharing%2520Tools%2520\(Premium\)%26utm_source%3Dt.co%26utm_medium%3Dreferral&text=Romo%20picks%20punctuate%20Cowboys%27%20collapse%20against%20Packers&via=houstonchron)[](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Romo%20picks%20punctuate%20Cowboys%27%20collapse%20against%20Packers%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.houstonchronicle.com%2Fsports%2Farticle%2Fromo-picks-punctuate-cowboys-collapse-against-5067516.php&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.houstonchronicle.com%2Fsports%2Farticle%2Fromo-picks-punctuate-cowboys-collapse-against-5067516.php%3Futm_campaign%3DCMS%2520Sharing%2520Tools%2520\(Premium\)%26utm_source%3Dbsky.app%26utm_medium%3Dreferral)[](mailto:?subject=Your%20friend%20has%20shared%20a%20Houston%20Chronicle%20link%20with%20you%3A&body=Romo%20picks%20punctuate%20Cowboys'%20collapse%20against%20Packers%0A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.houstonchronicle.com%2Fsports%2Farticle%2Fromo-picks-punctuate-cowboys-collapse-against-5067516.php%3Futm_campaign%3DCMS%2520Sharing%2520Tools%2520\(Premium\)%26utm_source%3Dshare-by-email%26utm_medium%3Demail%0A%0AThey%20were%20at%20home%2C%20the%20NFC%20East-leading%20Philadelphia%20Eagles%20had%20lost%20earlier%20in%20the%20day%2C%20and%20the%20visiting%20Green%20Bay%20Packers%20were%20without%20their%20Pro%20Bowl%20quarterback.%0A%0AThis%20message%20was%20sent%20via%20Houston%20Chronicle)

![Image 1: Tony Romo (9) and his Cowboys teammates were left to ponder how a 23-point halftime lead vanished on Sunday.](https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/article/romo-picks-punctuate-cowboys-collapse-against-5067516.php)

Tony Romo (9) and his Cowboys teammates were left to ponder how a 23-point halftime lead vanished on Sunday.

Tim Sharp/FRE

ARLINGTON - It was all there for the Dallas Cowboys' taking. They were at home, the NFC East-leading Philadelphia Eagles had lost earlier in the day, and the visiting Green Bay Packers were without their Pro Bowl quarterback.

And for a while, the Cowboys took full advantage. But then they reverted to being what they've been for so long in December and on many other occasions:

Chokers with a capital 'C.' Masters of the meltdown. Losers.

Advertisement

Article continues below this ad

With Tony Romo burnishing his reputation as a big-game dud by throwing two killer interceptions in the final 3 minutes, the Cowboys blew a 23-point third-quarter lead while unraveling 37-36 to the Packers on Sunday in a game that had playoff implications for both teams.

"This is unbelievable," Jerry Jones said after watching his team collapse even after grabbing an 11-point cushion with just under 8 minutes left on a spectacular 5-yard touchdown catch by Dez Bryant.

### 

Want more Houston Chronicle?

Make us a Preferred Source on Google to see more of us when you search.

[Add Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=houstonchronicle.com)

"I hate to have the taste I've got in my mouth. … This is one of the hardest losses I've ever experienced - a bitter, bitter disappointment."

But apparently not disappointing enough for Jones to reverse the vow he made last month that Jason Garrett will return next year as the star-crossed team's coach.

Advertisement

Article continues below this ad

Told he was being given a chance to slam the door on speculation Garrett would be fired if Dallas doesn't make the playoffs, a flustered Jones said, "I don't need a chance. I slammed that door back here four weeks ago. And you all shouldn't ask for (a vote of confidence for Garrett) every time you see me. … I was firm for one night (about Garrett returning), and that doesn't call for me having to be firm every morning I get up."

Despite the gut-wrenching defeat, the Cowboys (7-7) still control their destiny. If they beat the Redskins (3-11) and then the Eagles (8-6) in the regular-season finale on Dec. 29, they will advance to the playoffs for the first time since 2009.

But how realistic is that after Dallas has lost two straight, including a 45-28 drubbing in Chicago last week, and appears incapable of stopping any quarterback?

"I feel good we have a chance to beat the Redskins to get a chance to play Philadelphia (for the division title)," Jones said. "(If we win both games), you all will be asking me if I'm giving (Garrett) a raise, an extension."

After Minnesota upset Philadelphia earlier in the day, all the Cowboys needed to do to have a shot at clinching the division title next week was to beat the struggling Packers. But Green Bay (7-6-1) collected TDs on its first five possessions of the second half, outscoring Dallas 34-10 after the Cowboys had built a seemingly commanding 26-3 halftime lead.

Advertisement

Article continues below this ad

Filling in for injured Pro Bowler Aaron Rodgers, backup quarterback Matt Flynn shredded the NFL's worst defense for 299 yards and four touchdowns with one interception. The comeback matched the biggest in Packers history.

"What a feeling," Flynn said. "We were all just sitting around at the end taking knees. We were like, 'Is this real?' "

For the Cowboys, it was all too real and all too familiar. In 2011 at JerryWorld, the Detroit Lions returned two Romo interceptions for TDs en route to overcoming a 24-point third-quarter deficit for a 34-30 win. Romo's mistakes against the Packers weren't returned for scores, but they were just as devastating.

The first pick came on second-and-6 from the Dallas 35 with the Cowboys nursing a 36-31 lead. After checking out of a running play, Romo tried to hit Miles Austin over the middle only to have Sam Shields make the theft.

"They overloaded the side we were going to run to," Romo said, explaining why he changed the play. "It was my fault for putting the ball in a position where the defense could make a play."

Advertisement

Article continues below this ad

Seven plays later, the Cowboys allowed Eddie Lacy to score on a 1-yard run so they could get the ball back with 1:31 left and one timeout in their possession while trailing 37-36. But on the second play of the ensuing possession for Dallas, Tramon Williams made a diving interception at the Dallas 32 with 1:24 left.

Romo blamed that pick on a "miscommunication" with intended receiver Cole Beasley.

"It was disappointing," Garrett said. "None of us got the job done. We have to live with that reality."
